newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus accelerates work on stretched A340 planes.
newsitem.headline: Airbus accelerates work on stretched A340 planes.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said on Wednesday that its supervisory board had asked that studies being conducted on the A340-500 and the A340-600 -- stretched versions of the four-engined A340 aircraft -- be accelerated.

It asked for the studies to be speeded up "so as to obtain all necessary elements for a comprehensive assessment of these programmes by the end of the year prior to a launch decision," Airbus said in a statement.
The supervisory board made the request after meeting on Wednesday to review a report on studies being carried out on the planes.

The A340-600 will seat 376 passengers, while the A340-500 will carry 316 passengers. Airbus Industrie forecasts a need for over 3,600 aircraft in the 250-400 seat category. In broadening its product line with the proposed new versions, Airbus expects to grab at least 50 percent of the market. It now has a 45 percent share of the 250-300 seat market with its A330/A340 aircraft.

Airbus is a consortium of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
